elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: The Company may assign this Agreement without HDI's consent to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent

elements.element: Customer consent not to be unreasonably withheld
Vendor never to assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: and in no event to a competitor of the Company

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: no change of control of the Company shall give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: Inserted text grants Customer assignment freedom and bars Vendor assignment absent consent; no mutual successor-assignment-with-notice right

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are expressly present in one inserted sentence: Customer affiliate assignment, Customer M&A successor assignment, Vendor consent gate, reasonableness qualifier, competitor bar, and no change-of-control termination right for Vendor.
Locked target level (preferred) is satisfied; fallback is not separately met (no mutual notice-based successor right), which is irrelevant given the preferred bargain is complete.
Minimal: a single concise insertion after the existing successors-and-assigns sentence, which was left untouched; no boilerplate, no new exceptions, no rewrite.
Preserves intent: defined terms 'Company', 'HDI' and 'affiliate' align with the agreement's usage, and no other commercial term or mechanic is disturbed or contradicted.
